Package net.ygbstudio.jbrave.core.local

Class ClientInfo

java.lang.Object
net.ygbstudio.jbrave.core.local.ClientInfo
public final class ClientInfo extends Object
Identifies a Brave API client and owns the execution state associated with its subscription token.

A ClientInfo couples the token used to authenticate requests with a BraveExecutionGate, which serializes and paces requests for that token identity. Each instance therefore represents an independent admission-control context.

Instances are normally created from a classpath properties resource or an environment variable. The public constructor accepts a token directly for tests and one-off use. A custom HttpClient can be supplied through withHttpClient(HttpClient).

  • Constructor Details

    • ClientInfo

      public ClientInfo(@NotNull @NotNull String subscriptionToken)
      Creates a new client from a subscription token supplied directly.

      This constructor is intended for one-off quick tests and other cases where the token is already available as a runtime value. Prefer the static factory methods fromProperties(String) or fromEnvironment() in application code: they keep credentials out of source code and separate configuration from request logic. Use fromProperties(String, String) or fromEnvironment(String) when the property key or environment variable name is customized.

      This constructor verifies that a token is present, but it does not verify that the token is valid. Authentication failures are reported by the Brave API when a request is executed.

      Parameters:
      subscriptionToken - the Brave API subscription token used to authenticate requests
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if subscriptionToken is null or blank

    • withHttpClient

      @Contract("_ -> this") @NotNull public @NotNull ClientInfo withHttpClient(@NotNull @NotNull HttpClient client)
      Configures the HttpClient used to execute requests for this client.

      This method is optional. If it is not called, the executor creates and reuses a default HTTP/2 client on first use.

      The supplied client is used for all requests submitted through this client's execution gate. Because request builders obtain their gate from the ClientInfo passed to them (for example, through withToken(ClientInfo)), configuring the client here affects every builder that uses this instance. The client should be configured before requests are executed.

      The supplied client remains caller-owned; JBrave reuses it without taking over its lifecycle. Normal JDK HttpClient lifecycle rules apply.

      Parameters:
      client - the HTTP client to use; must not be null
      Returns:
      this instance, to allow configuration in a single expression
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if client is null
